question.problem:
$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,1)=\{\begin{aligned}0.4, & x=1 \\ 0.6, & x=2 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Suppose $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables. Find the conditional variance $\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=1]$ given that the conditional probability mass function ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,1)$ is shown above and the corresponding conditional expected value is ${\mu }_{X|1}=1.6.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the conditional variance of $X$ given $Y=y$ is defined by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=y] & =\text{E}[(X-{\mu }_{X|y})^{2}\,|\,Y=y] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}\,|\,Y=y]-{\mu }_{X|y}^{2} \\  & =[{\sum }_{x}{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)]-{\mu }_{X|y}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X\,|\,Y=y] & =[{\sum }_{x}{x}^{2}\,{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,1)]-{\mu }_{X|1}^{2} \\  & =[(1)^{2}\cdot 0.4+(2)^{2}\cdot 0.6]-(1.6)^{2} \\  & =0.4+2.4-2.56 \\  & =0.24.\end{aligned}
$$
